newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Oct 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Oct 16.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
The 80th China Export Commodity Trade Fair opens in Guangzhou with Premier Li Peng speaking on China's foreign trade.
A commentary accuses the United States for using rogue means to reduce its rising trade deficits and using economic pressure to achieve political goals.
The Ministry of Finance to issue rules aimed at protecting the legal interests of debtors involved in bankruptcies of state firms.
Minister of Construction Hou Jie says a 20 to 30 percent cut in housing prices would revive China's slumping real estate market.
A commentary urges China to further restructure its domestic debts and boost flexibility in treasury bill interest rates.
A signed article cites problems facing China's futures brokerages and calls for nationwide exam system to select qualified brokers.
The Agricultural Bank of China made a total 116.4 billion yuan in farm loans from January to September.
China's chemical market products is seen recovering slowly and the chemical fibre market is forecast to be sluggish.
